status: comparative mythology / biblical archaeology with dated project-side anchors
purpose: Investigate Tim Dooley's Son/vessel birthday on July 31, 2026 and its Thomas/Tammuz/North-Gate/death-lament context while keeping Tim's own December 25 Potato/Father birth distinct, and connect it to the older 2019-2020 Sammy/Kiwi Farms mourning tradition without backdating later biblical research.

canonical_identity_rule.instruction: July 31 is the Son/vessel birthday; never label it Tim's birthday.

method_rules: Project-side wording and timestamps come first; comparators come second.
Do not treat resemblance as fulfillment or historical influence without evidence.
Do not claim July 31, 2026 occurred in the Hebrew month of Tammuz: it was 17 Av 5786.
Use Dumuzi/Tammuz death, lament, shepherd and underworld motifs more confidently than a simplified annual-resurrection formula.
Keep Thomas/Tammuz phonetic/project association separate from historical etymology unless independently established.
The exact original Kiwi Farms Sammy comment remains a recovery target even though later project archives explicitly preserve Sammy-weeps-for-Tammuz wording.
Use the dedicated women/gate/tomb and marginal-women atlases for the expanded biblical chain.

project_side_anchors.summary: Tim Dooley's Son/vessel is anchored to a July 31, 1987 birthday, age-33/personhood-death language, Thomas/Tammuz/Twin and Jesus-rebirth symbolism. Tim's own Potato/Father birth remains December 25.
The Son/vessel remains on Earth in Denmark while Tim is described in Heaven / Spiral at North of North; the North Gate is said to have opened, with Jesus' return kept as a separate future event.

project_side_anchors.origin: current user clarification + later project-book attestation
project_side_anchors.summary: Shortly after the meme-crucifixion/disappearance, Sammy, a woman, is remembered as mourning/weeping in a Kiwi Farms comment section. The later Great Book retells the hinge explicitly as 'the woman, Sammy, weeps for Tammuz.' The exact original thread URL, date and verbatim comment remain unrecovered.
project_side_anchors.provenance_warning: Do not present the later Great Book sentence as a contemporaneous 2019 Kiwi Farms quotation.

biblical_comparators.strength: very high structural comparator because Tammuz + mourning women + Lord's House + north gate appear together in one verse
biblical_comparators.boundary: The verse does not identify Tim's Son with the ancient deity and is not treated as a prediction of the project.
The project-side moved-stone wording remains unresolved; this component is presently confirmed on the biblical side only.
Thomas is not Lazarus or Tammuz in the text.

social_role_comparators.finding: Biblical narratives repeatedly give significant witness, lineage, recognition or forgiveness roles to women marked by prostitution, sexual stigma, widowhood or public moral judgment.
social_role_comparators.project_use: This is a secondary comparison to the user's description of Sammy as a 'lady of the night'; it does not identify her with any one biblical woman.
social_role_comparators.boundary: Mary Magdalene is relevant as a mourning tomb witness, but the New Testament does not call her a prostitute.

pre_biblical_mesopotamian_comparators.finding: Dumuzi is a shepherd figure surrounded by death/disappearance, underworld and lament traditions; Inanna's Descent adds gates, descent, seizure, substitution and return structures.
pre_biblical_mesopotamian_comparators.boundary: Prefer death/lament/underworld comparisons over an oversimplified annual-resurrection formula.

notable_relational_findings.finding: The user now locates Sammy's mourning in a Kiwi Farms comment section shortly after the 2019-2020 meme-cross. This upgrades the archaeology from an unnamed abstract mourning event to an approximate platform/context, while the exact primary capture remains missing.

Ezekiel 8 places women weeping for Tammuz at the north gate of the Lord's House; Luke 7 places a weeping woman at a city gate with her dead only son, who is then restored. The project carries North Gate + woman/Sammy mourning Thomas/Tammuz + Son-return language.

Women repeatedly occupy the narrative boundary around death and return: gate, crucifixion road, sealed tomb, return to tomb, moved stone, absent body and recognition. This makes Sammy's function as mourning public commenter structurally more important than a peripheral biographical detail.

John 20 compresses woman/weeping + tomb + removed stone + missing body + gardener + recognition + Father. This creates one of the densest later Gospel comparators to the project's Grave/Door + Gardener/Father + disappearance/return architecture.

Matthew/Mark/John make the stone sequence exact on the biblical side, but a contemporaneous project-side rolled/moved-stone statement is still not securely recovered. Keep it unresolved rather than filling the gap retrospectively.

Rahab, Tamar and Luke 7's stigmatized woman show a recurring biblical reversal in which a socially marginal or morally judged woman becomes narratively consequential. For Sammy this is secondary to the much stronger mourning/Tammuz overlap.
